findings.title: Off-by-one slice drops the newest invoice on every page
findings.explanation: `rows.slice(1, limit + 1)` skips the first row, which is the newest invoice. Every page therefore loses one invoice and returns only `limit - 1` items when more pages exist. When `rows.length` is `limit + 1`, `slice(1, limit + 1)` returns `limit` rows and still omits `rows[0]`. Because `next_before` is taken from the last row of the slice, the cursor stays correct, so the omitted invoice is never fetched by any later request. Use `rows.slice(0, limit)`.

findings.title: No test coverage for the pagination boundary cases
findings.explanation: The change targets an edge case (last page exactly full) and the bug above would have been caught by a basic test. Add tests for these cases: fewer than `limit` rows, exactly `limit` rows (`next_before` must be null), `limit + 1` rows (`next_before` set, and the first row present in the response), and a follow-up request using the returned cursor.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Fix next_before when the last page is exactly full

When the last page had exactly `limit` invoices, `next_before` was still set, so the web app made one extra request that came back empty. This fetches `limit + 1` rows to know whether another page exists.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts
index b9edb19..8e99e4e 100644
--- a/src/routes/invoices.ts
+++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts
@@ -19,11 +19,13 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/', async (req, res) => {
       WHERE org_id = $1 AND ($2::bigint IS NULL OR id < $2)
       ORDER BY id DESC
       LIMIT $3`,
-    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit],
+    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit + 1],
   )
+  const hasMore = rows.length > limit
+  const page = rows.slice(1, limit + 1)
   res.json({
-    invoices: rows.map(serializeInvoice),
-    next_before: rows.length === limit ? rows[rows.length - 1].id : null,
+    invoices: page.map(serializeInvoice),
+    next_before: hasMore ? page[page.length - 1].id : null,
   })
 })
```
